title: Create src/lib/parser/jsonStream.ts — output stream parser
description: Create a parser that processes stdout lines from AI backends. Tries to parse each line as JSON, returning the parsed object if successful or a text object if not. Handles partial JSON buffered across multiple lines.
acceptanceCriteria: Valid JSON lines are parsed and returned as parsed objects
Non-JSON lines are returned as { type: 'text', content: line }
Partial JSON split across multiple lines is buffered and assembled
Empty lines are handled gracefully (return null)

steps.details: Create the file. Define types: export type ParsedLine = { type: 'json'; data: unknown } | { type: 'text'; content: string }

Export: function createJsonStreamParser(): { process(line: string): ParsedLine | null } { let buffer = ''; return { process(line: string): ParsedLine | null { if (!line.trim()) return null; buffer += line; try { const data = JSON.parse(buffer); buffer = ''; return { type: 'json', data }; } catch { if (buffer.startsWith('{') || buffer.startsWith('[')) return null; // partial JSON, keep buffering buffer = ''; return { type: 'text', content: line }; } } } }

steps.description: Handle buffer reset on non-JSON text
steps.details: Ensure that if a line cannot be the start of JSON (doesn't start with { or [), the buffer is cleared and the line is returned as text immediately. This prevents the buffer from growing indefinitely.

technicalNotes: JSON.parse throws SyntaxError on invalid JSON — catch it and determine if we're in mid-stream or have a non-JSON line
The factory pattern allows multiple independent parsers to coexist (e.g., one per backend stream)
